== Research Notes ==

A possible identification concerns Robert Glasgow, Cookstown inn and Academy notices. Robert Glasgow was the named Cookstown contact for letting the King’s Arms Inn in October 1836. A 1840 Cookstown Academy advertisement names Robert Glasgow as chairman of its superintending committee and an applicant contact for a teacher.<ref>Belfast News-Letter, 18 October 1836, p. 3, King’s Arms Inn letting; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/390551780/ record]; Belfast News-Letter, 30 October 1840, p. 2, Cookstown Academy; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/390563103/ record]; Belfast News-Letter, 20 November 1840, p. 3, reprint of Cookstown Academy notice dated 28 October; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/390563666/ record].</ref> The notices name roles, not his age or family. The 1836 contact is not explicitly described as innkeeper or owner. The Academy is not described as a Sunday school. Consolidated as a same-name Cookstown research account; identity between the notices, the mill partner, [[Glasgow-2656]] and [[Glasgow-3941]] remains unproved. Neither notice identifies the already-deceased father of the surgeon. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns Robert Glasgow, Loughinsholin freeholder, 1831. The 16 August 1831 declaration lists Robert Glasgow and John Glasgow among freeholders of the barony printed Loughinshollen (modern Loughinsholin), County Londonderry, supporting Sir Robert Bateson. They are co-signatories; no kinship, occupation, age or individual townland is given. Castledawson and 4 July 1831 refer to the opposing meeting discussed in the declaration, not their homes or their signing date.<ref>Belfast News-Letter, 16 August 1831, p.3, Loughinshollen freeholders’ declaration; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/390548642/ record].</ref> [[Glasgow-3941|Robert Glasgow]], the Coltrim land occupier documented in 1820–1831, is a strong compatible regional candidate; the newspaper lacks a townland or family bridge to prove it. [[Glasgow-2656]] of the Cookstown district remains another adult comparison. [[Glasgow-12]] has an Ohio record sequence and is a weaker comparison despite Moneymore origin; the newspaper does not resolve his travel or retained Irish property. No Robert is identified as John’s father or brother, or as the surgeon’s father, from this signature. The identification remains uncertain.
